questions.q: What is the relationship between geo-replication and the failover group from Lessons 12-13?
options: They are unrelated, competing features
Geo-replication only works after a failover group is deleted
Geo-replication is the data-movement engine; the failover group is the endpoint-management layer built on top of it
The failover group replaces the need for geo-replication entirely
questions.explain: The failover group uses geo-replication underneath to actually move the data — it adds the stable listener endpoint on top.

questions.q: Why is active geo-replication asynchronous rather than synchronous?
options: Synchronous replication isn't technically possible across regions
There is no real reason; it's an arbitrary default
Synchronous replication would wait for the distant secondary to confirm every write, adding real latency to every transaction — asynchronous keeps that off the critical path
Asynchronous replication is required by Azure regulations
questions.explain: Asynchronous replication is a deliberate trade-off: lower latency for every write, at the cost of a small replication lag window.

questions.q: How does asynchronous replication directly connect to Lesson 11's 5-minute RPO target?
options: RPO is set by Azure automatically and can't be chosen
It doesn't connect at all
The 5-minute RPO is Overlook explicitly acknowledging that asynchronous replication's small lag is an acceptable cost in exchange for not slowing down every write
A 5-minute RPO requires synchronous replication
questions.explain: Setting RPO above zero is a direct acknowledgment of the replication lag inherent in asynchronous geo-replication.

questions.q: Why does Overlook's secondary server live in a different Azure region rather than just a different server in the same datacenter?
options: So a region-wide outage, not just a single server or datacenter failure, doesn't take down both the primary and secondary at once
It's required by Azure licensing
There is no real reason for this choice
Different regions are always cheaper
questions.explain: Choosing a genuinely independent failure domain is the whole point of geo-replication over a local HA mechanism.

questions.q: What cost/benefit trade-off does this lesson say the board should understand about the readable secondary?
options: It is entirely free and adds no ongoing cost
It's a second provisioned database with its own ongoing cost, but it can also serve read-only reporting traffic in normal operation, offloading load from the primary
It can only ever be used for disaster recovery, never for any other purpose
It automatically reduces the primary's cost to zero
questions.explain: The secondary is a real ongoing cost, but it has a real additional benefit beyond pure DR — worth explaining in plain terms when presenting cost to leadership.
